h1: Commercial Painting for Micanopy Shops and Storefronts
heroIntro: Micanopy's antique shops and small commercial buildings are part of what draws visitors to town. We repaint them carefully, on a schedule that keeps your doors open.

sections.h2: Storefronts that set the tone for the town
body: In a town known for antique shops and oak-lined streets, a storefront's paint is part of the visitor experience. Faded trim, peeling door frames, or mildew streaks on a facade stand out more here than they would in a strip center. Commercial painting in Micanopy, FL is about keeping those older buildings looking cared for without making them look new in the wrong way.
These buildings also come with age-related issues: many layers of old paint on wood trim and doors, masonry or stucco with hairline cracks, and shaded walls that grow mildew under the canopy.

Small offices, galleries, and service businesses in town get the same treatment. Whether the building is an old storefront or a converted house, we start by finding out which coatings are still sound and where water is getting in, then build the scope around what the building needs.

Antique shops are full of fragile, valuable, and often heavy merchandise. Interior painting in that setting means planning: we work section by section, cover display pieces in place where moving them is risky, and coordinate with you on what can be shifted and when. Drop cloths and masking go down before any sanding or painting, and work areas are cleaned each day.

We schedule commercial work around operating hours, including nights and weekends, so you can keep selling while the space improves. On the outside, prep and painting can be phased elevation by elevation so the entrance is always open.

bullets: Wood storefront trim, doors, and window frames: 100% acrylic, or waterborne urethane enamel on high-touch doors and railings
Stucco with hairline movement: elastomeric that bridges small cracks
Brick and block: a masonry system chosen after the walkthrough
Interior sales floors and offices: low-VOC, washable finishes
body: For larger stucco damage, stucco repair can be part of the scope. Masonry details are on our concrete and masonry painting page.

We are licensed, bonded, and fully insured in Florida, with workers' comp on every crew member. A certificate of insurance naming your business, landlord, or property manager is available before we start. Our own crews do the work, and one crew lead is your contact from walkthrough to punch walk. The written scope lists every surface, product, coat, and schedule phase, and nothing changes without your written approval.
Color choices for storefronts benefit from on-site testing; see our Micanopy color consultation. More on our commercial work is on the retail and restaurant painting page.

faqs.q: Do I need to empty my antique shop before you paint inside?
faqs.a: No. We work in sections, cover pieces in place where moving them is risky, and coordinate with you on anything that needs to be shifted.

faqs.q: Can you paint my storefront outside of business hours?
faqs.a: Yes. Commercial work is scheduled around your operating hours, including nights and weekends.

faqs.q: Will you provide a certificate of insurance for my landlord?
faqs.a: Yes. We can issue a certificate of insurance naming your entity, landlord, or property manager before mobilization.
